_about: Fees & taxes reference for a paper wallet of an Israeli resident individual. Numbers are copied from the cited sources; fields with "verified": false or a "caveat" were not confirmed against a primary source. Broker prices are LIST prices unless marked promo; Israeli banks negotiate personally.

tax.substantial_shareholder_def: holds 10% or more of the company

surtax.threshold_note: Frozen (no CPI linkage) for 2025-2027 per secondary sources.
surtax.applies_to: Annual taxable income from ALL sources above the threshold (3%). From 2025, an extra 2% on the part of capital income (capital gains, dividends, interest, etc.) above the same threshold.

tax.real_vs_nominal: Tax is on the REAL gain: nominal gain minus the 'inflationary amount'. The inflationary amount accrued after 1994-01-01 is exempt for individuals (pre-1994 part taxed at 10%).
tax.foreign_currency_rule: Individual holding a foreign-currency security: everything is measured in ILS. Cost is converted at the Bank of Israel representative rate on the purchase date and proceeds at the rate on the sale date -> nominal ILS gain. For such a security the exchange rate is 'deemed the index', so the inflationary amount is the currency move on the cost and is exempt. In practice: real gain = (sale_usd - cost_usd) * fx_sale. Edge cases (secondary sources, verify): if nominal ILS gain > 0 but the USD-based real gain is larger (shekel strengthened), tax only the nominal ILS gain; if nominal ILS gain > 0 but USD result is a loss, gain is exempt (taxable 0); if nominal ILS result is a loss, the ILS nominal loss is the capital loss. Simplified engine rule: taxable = max(0, min(nominal_ils_gain, usd_gain * fx_sale)) when nominal >= 0, else loss = nominal_ils_gain.
tax.fx_rate_source: Bank of Israel representative rate (sha'ar yatzig) on trade date
tax.loss_offset: Capital losses offset capital gains in the same tax year (Israeli or foreign; a loss on a foreign asset is first set against foreign-source gains). Securities losses may also offset interest/dividends from securities in the same year if the tax rate on that income does not exceed 25%. Unused losses carry forward indefinitely, but only against future capital gains. An Israeli broker offsets gains/losses automatically within the account during the year; across brokers you offset via the annual return.

withholding_vs_self_report.israeli_broker: Withholds 25% at source on realized real gain (and on dividends), offsetting losses within the account during the year. No annual return required if all was withheld and no surtax applies (verify: annual return still needed in some cases, e.g. surtax, multiple accounts).
withholding_vs_self_report.foreign_broker: Foreign brokers (e.g. Interactive Brokers) do not withhold Israeli tax and do not report to the Israel Tax Authority. The investor must file a semi-annual report and pay an advance on net securities gains by 31 July (for Jan-Jun) and 31 January (for Jul-Dec), and file an annual return (form 1301 + appendix 1322 for capital gains, 1324 for foreign income/dividends with foreign tax credit).

dividends.foreign_tax_credit: Foreign tax withheld is credited against the Israeli 25%, up to the Israeli tax on that dividend. If foreign withholding > 25%, the excess is not credited (only recoverable by a reclaim in the source country under a treaty). Israeli brokers typically withhold only the difference up to 25% (not verified from a primary source).

US.note: With W-8BEN the US-Israel treaty rate for individuals is 25% (NOT 15%). 12.5% only for a company owning >=10% of voting shares. No W-8BEN -> 30%.

JP.note: PwC chart: 15% for non-residents on listed shares; +2.1% reconstruction surtax gives 15.315% (surtax not in PwC chart - from general knowledge, verify).

DE.note: 25% + 5.5% solidarity surcharge. Partly reclaimable down to the treaty rate.

CH.note: Statutory 35%; reclaim to treaty rate possible via Swiss forms (slow). Excess over 25% is lost for Israeli credit unless reclaimed.

KR.note: PwC chart: 20%; plus 10% local income tax surcharge = 22% (surcharge from general knowledge, verify).

FR.note: PwC: 12.8% for non-resident individuals (25% for companies). GlobeTax lists 25% (US-investor/corporate basis). Use 12.8% for individuals; verify.

dividends.note: Rates are statutory for non-residents; Israel's treaty with each country may cap them lower, but brokers often withhold the statutory rate and the investor must reclaim.

brokers.name: Interactive Brokers (IBKR Pro Fixed, direct account)

us.note: Fixed plan; SEC fee and FINRA TAF/CAT are passed through on sales. Tiered alternative: 0.0035/share, min 0.35, plus exchange/clearing fees. IBKR Lite ($0) is generally not available to Israeli residents (verify).

tase.note: Fixed 0.1% of trade value, min ILS 15. Tiered: 0.05%, min ILS 5.25, max ILS 120 + third-party fees.

eu.note: Fixed, SmartRouting, Germany/NL/FR/UK/CH/DK. Direct routing is 0.10% with higher minimums. Taxes (UK stamp, FR/IT FTT) are extra.

brokers.fx_note: Manual conversion: 0.002% (0.2 bp) of value, min USD 2, no added spread (interbank rate). Auto-conversion pricing reported differently (~0.03%) by secondary sources - unverified.
brokers.note: Official IBKR schedule downloaded 2026-11-12. No custody or inactivity fee. Does not withhold Israeli tax -> semi-annual self-reporting.

brokers.note: Per TheMarker Supermarker comparison (updated 10/2026). TASE fee 'not provided'. Different from direct IBKR pricing.

brokers.monthly_fee_note: PROMO: handling fee waived 4 years (new clients), afterwards offset against commissions. Tariff allows raising it (up to ILS 90/month per TheMarker).

US_sale_sec_fee.note: $20.60 per $1M of sales (FY2026). Rate was $0 before 2026-04-04.

US_sale_finra_taf.note: 2026 schedule. FINRA filed SR-FINRA-2026-021 to pause TAF for trades 2026-10-01..2026-12-31; IBKR's schedule currently shows TAF USD 0.00 per share sold. 2027 rate scheduled at 0.000232 (max 11.61) but SR-FINRA-2026-020 proposes keeping 2026 rates for 2027-2028.

UK_stamp.note: SDRT on UK-incorporated shares. AIM shares exempt; new UK listings relieved for 3 years from 2025-11-27. Plus GBP 1.50 PTM levy on trades > GBP 10,000 (verify).

FR_ftt.note: French companies with market cap > EUR 1bn (annual list). Rate raised 0.3% -> 0.4% in 2025.

IT_ftt.note: From 2026-01-01 (Budget Law 199/2025): 0.2% on regulated markets, 0.4% OTC. Issuers < EUR 500m cap exempt. A 2027 draft would double again - unconfirmed.

HK_stamp.note: 0.1% per side since 2023-11-17 (cut from 0.13%). Other HK levies (SFC, AFRC, exchange trading fee) not researched.

TW_stt.note: Stocks 0.3%; ETFs 0.1%. IBKR passes it to the seller.

KR_stt.note: 2026: ~0.20% incl. agriculture & fishery special tax on KOSPI; sources conflict on the split (0.05% + 0.15%).

CN_stamp.note: A-shares 0.05% seller-side since Aug 2023 - from general knowledge, NOT verified in this session.

IL_tase.note: No stamp duty / FTT on TASE trades.
